questions.question: The 'Friendship Highway' is a road that connects China to ______.
questions.solution:
• The **'Friendship Highway' **also **known as the China-Nepal Highway**, connects the **capital of Tibet, Lhasa **with the **Nepalese-Chinese border **between **Zhangmu and Kodari**.
 
• The 800-kilometre long 'Friendship Highway' goes through the Himalayan mountains and along the **Yarlung valley **upto **Shigatse**, **Tibet's second-largest city **and formerly the **home of the Panchen Lamas**.

questions.question: Which Indian author wrote the book 'The English Teacher'?
questions.solution:
__
 
• The **English Teacher is a 1945 novel written by R. K. Narayan.__ **It is the third and final part in the 'Malgudi Days" series, preceded by Swami and Friends (1935) and The Bachelor of Arts (1937).
 
• This novel, dedicated to Narayan's wife Rajam is not only autobiographical but also poignant in its intensity of feeling.
 
• The story is a series of experiences in the life of Krishna, an English teacher, and his quest towards achieving inner peace and self - development.

questions.question: In which province of China is the Huangguoshu National Park located which houses the world's largest waterfall cluster.
questions.solution:

questions.question: Who among the following is the only Indian to have won the Amateur World title in both, snooker and billiards?
questions.solution:
• **Pankaj Advani** is the **only Indian **to have **won the Amateur World title in both**, **snooker and billiards**.

• Pankaj Advani has also won country's most prestigious awards **Padma Shri in 2009**, **Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna in 2006 **and **Arjuna Award in 2004**.

questions.question: _______ assumed the title of 'Gangaikondachola', or the conqueror of the river Ganga.
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Indian king Rajendra Chola-I**__ used naval powers to conquer parts of Eastasia.
 
• He defeated Sri Vijaya or the Kadaram kingdom in East Asia and bore the title Kadaramkonda.
 
• He belongs to the Imperial Chola Dynasty.
 
• His reign was from 1012-1044 A.D.
 
• He built a city called Gangaikonda Cholapuram to commemorate his victory in his northern India campaign which spanned up to Ganges River, where he defeated Bengal king Mahipala-I.
 
• Therefore, he assumed the title of 'Gangaikondachola' or the conqueror of the river Ganga.

questions.question: When was the Constitution of Pakistan enforced?
questions.solution:

• After partitioned from India, Pakistan was **declared as an Islamic Republic **and it was made **mandatory **that **only a Muslim could become the President of the country**.

questions.question: Which of the following was a port city of the Indus Valley Civilization?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Lothal__ **is a port city in Gujarat, located on the banks of the Bhogava River, a right tributary of the Sabarmati River.
 
• It had the earliest known dock in the world, used mainly for trade purposes in the Indus Valley Civilization.
 
• Lothal is situated in the Ahmedabad District in modern Gujarat.
 
• It is considered a port town according to the Archaeological Survey of India.

questions.question: In which part of the flower does fertilisation take place?
questions.solution:
• **Carpels,** present in the centre of a flower, form the female reproductive part. It is surrounded by male reproductive structures called stamens.
 
• The carpels and stamens are surrounded by petals.
 
• The petals are protected by sepals, which are green.
 
• The carpels are the female reproductive part of the flower. It is divided into three parts namely- ovary, style and stigma.
 
• The** ovary contains ovules and the style acts as a passage for the pollen tubes **carrying the male gametes.
 
• The stigma is the terminal part of the carpel which is receptive and it receives the pollen grains and provides nutrition for the growth and development of the pollen tube which carries male gametes through style and reaches the ovules to fertilise an egg.

questions.question: About 70% of the sun is made up of ______.
questions.solution:

• It is one of most **important sources of energy for life on earth**.

questions.question: DNA is stored majorly in ______ of the cell.

questions.question: The 'Tanakh' is the sacred text of which religion/sect?
questions.solution:
• The Torah is part of the larger text known as the Tanakh or the Hebrew Bible.
 
• ‘The Torah’ is the central reference of Judaism. It has a range of meanings. It can most specifically mean the first five books of the 24 books of the Tanakh, and it usually includes the rabbinic commentaries.
 
• It is supplemental oral tradition represented by later texts such as the Midrash and the Talmud.
 
• With between 14.5 and 17.4 million adherents worldwide, Judaism is the tenth largest religion in the world.

questions.question: In 2019, Harsh Vardhan, the union minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change launched the India Cooling Action Plan (ICAP). On which day was ICAP released?
questions.solution:
• Ministry for Environment, Forest and Climate Change launched ';India Cooling Action Plan' (ICAP) on 8 March 2019.
 
• ICAP is a 20-year road map (2018 to 2038) to address the cooling requirements for all sectors such as buildings, cold chain, transport and refrigeration.
 
• It aims to reduce cooling demand across sectors by 20% to 25% and reduce refrigerant demand by 25% to 30% by 2037-38.

questions.question: The phrase 'Survival of the fittest' as a way of describing the mechanism of natural selection was coined by ______.
questions.solution:
__
 
• **‘Survival of the fittest’** is a phrase that comes from the principle of natural selection which was given by Charles Darwin.
 
• The phrase was actually **used first by** **Herbert Spencer**__ after reading Darwin’s book ‘On the Origin of Species’.
 
• It originated from the Darwinian Evolutionary theory and reproductive success is the biological concept of it.
 
• In simpler terms, it means, that the form which will leave the most copies of itself in the successive generations will survive.

questions.question: The interest rate charged by banks on short-term loans to their largest, most secure and most creditworthy customers is called ______.
questions.solution:
• Benchmark prime lending rate or ;prime rate is the interest rate that commercial banks charge their most creditworthy customers.
 
• Prime lending rate, is largely determined by the federal funds rate, which is the overnight rate that banks use to lend to one another.
 
• The prime rate is also important for individual borrowers, as the prime rate directly affects the lending rates available for a mortgage, small business loan or personal loan.
 
• Generally, the prime rate is reserved for only the most qualified customers, determined as those who pose the least amount of risk of default. 
 
• RBI's REPO rate and CRR affect the benchmark prime lending rate.

questions.question: World Water Day is annually celebrated on ______.
questions.solution:
__
 
• World Water Day is celebrated annually on **22nd March.**__
 
• The day aims to draw attention to the importance of universal access to clean water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) facilities in developing countries. 
 
• The day also focuses on advocating for the sustainable management of freshwater resources.
 
• Theme: "Leaving no one behind".
 
• This is an adaptation of the central promise of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development: as sustainable development progresses, everyone must benefit.

questions.question: Which one of the following is the highest altitude lake of Pakistan?
questions.solution:
• The **highest lake in Pakistan **is the **Rush Lake **located in **Nagar Valley**, **Gilgit - Baltistan **at an **altitude of over 4,700 meters **near the **Rush Pari Peak**.
 
• It is also the **25th highest lake is the world**.
 
• The **second highest lake in Pakistan **is the **Karambar Lake**, which at an **altitude of 4,272 meters**, is the **31st highest lake in the world**.
 
• It is also **one of the highest alpine lakes in the world**.

questions.question: The Constitution of India was amended for the first time in which year?
questions.solution:
• The **Constitution of India **was amended for the **first time on 10th May 1951**.
 
• The **Statement of Objects and Reasons **appended to the **Constitution (First Amendment) Bill, 1951 **was **enacted as the Constitution (First Amendment) Act, 1951**.
 
• The **first amendment added Article 15(4) and Article 19(6) **and also brought **changes in the right to property **in pursuance after the decision of Supreme Court **regarding Fundamental Right of the Citizens**.
